glass: small stemmed wine glass (about 200 ml), chilled, no ice
version: v1 (round 4, 2026-10-01): an El Presidente (Oxford EL PRESIDENTE pdf 715-716: white Cuban rum, sweet white vermouth, 5 ml each orange curaçao and grenadine, stirred, up, orange twist and cherry; Imbibe! pdf 216-217: Constante's vermouth de Chambéry, Dolin Blanc 'the last survivor', half a barspoon of grenadine; Joy pdf 283: 1 tsp curaçao, 1/2 tsp grenadine), one of the two drinks Conigliaro aged in glass (Proper p. 228). The change: 10 ml rainwater Madeira in part of the vermouth's place, because Conigliaro's question came from wine (Oxford BARREL-AGED COCKTAILS pdf 216). Proportions mine: rum about 2.4 to 1 over the wines (Imbibe! pdf 216 calls the Presidente the Cubans' answer to the Manhattan), because Oxford's equal parts reads OUT high on sugar and acid; curaçao up to 7.5 ml (sugar without acid), grenadine at Wondrich's and Regan's half spoon (2.5 ml). Cherry left off (mine). Swept 4374 points: rum 37.5-45%, blanc 10-16 g, Madeira sugar 2-8 g x acid 0.5-0.9%, curaçao 30-40% x 20-35 g, grenadine 55-80 g x acid 0.3-1.0%: OUT only in the corner Madeira acid 0.9 with grenadine acid 1.0 together.
